transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

I came in because I keep getting these nagging thoughts at work, like I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout or maybe sent the wrong version to a client. Even when I can look at it and tell myself it’s probably fine, my mind keeps circling back to it, and it’s been hard to just let it go.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about other things in your life, not just these thoughts about mistakes at work?

Not really, or at least I haven’t noticed it in the same way. It mostly seems tied to the work mistakes and whether I missed something. Outside of that, I’m not sure—I don’t think I’m generally worried about everything.
When these thoughts come up, do you find yourself doing anything specific, like checking things over and over or following certain steps, to make sure everything is right?

Yes. Before I submit something now, I’ll usually re-open the file and go through it again. I compare the layers, re-save it, and sometimes I sort of mentally walk through every design choice one more time.

It’s not like it takes over my whole day, but it definitely slows me down, and I feel less free creatively because I’m second-guessing things.
Do these thoughts and checking behaviors interfere with your ability to do your job or affect other areas of your life, like relationships or free time?

I’m still getting my work done, but it is starting to affect things. I’ve missed a few internal deadlines because I keep checking and reworking files before I feel okay sending them along.

And I think it’s making me play it safer creatively. Like, I’ll avoid bolder ideas because I’m worried I’ll miss some detail and it’ll reflect badly on me. That bothers me because I’m trying to move toward a creative director role, and I feel like this could hurt my chances if it keeps going.
Have you noticed any other types of intrusive or unwanted thoughts that come up outside of work situations, things that bother you even if they don’t relate to your job performance?

Not really outside of work, no. The main thing is still that nagging thought that I missed some tiny mistake in a layout or sent the wrong version to a client. Even when I look at it and can tell it’s probably fine, my mind keeps coming back to it.
Do these thoughts and the checking you do cause you significant distress, or make it hard for you to function the way you’d like at work or in other areas of your life?

Yes, it does cause me distress. I’m still managing to get my work done, but not as smoothly as I used to. I’ve started missing some internal deadlines because I keep checking things before I send them.

And I’m noticing I hold back on bigger or bolder design ideas because I’m scared I’ll miss something and it’ll look bad. That worries me, especially because I’m trying to move toward a creative director role, and I don’t want this to get in the way.
Have you ever had any intrusive or unwanted thoughts that seem strange or upsetting to you, even if they don’t relate to your work or missing mistakes?

No, not really strange thoughts outside of that. It’s more the same work-related loop — like I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or I sent the wrong version to a client. Even after I check and it looks fine, my mind keeps going back to it.
Do you ever find yourself doing anything else physically, like tapping, counting, or repeating actions a certain number of times, to feel more at ease or make sure things are right?

Not really tapping or counting, no. It’s more with the files themselves. Before I submit something, I’ll re-open it, compare the layers, re-save it, and sometimes mentally walk through every design choice one more time. It doesn’t take over my whole day, but it does slow me down and makes me feel less free creatively.
Do you ever have intrusive thoughts or feel the need to do certain mental rituals even when you're not working or thinking about work tasks?

Not really outside of work. The intrusive thoughts are pretty much about my design files — like I missed a tiny mistake in a layout or sent the wrong version to a client. Even when I can see it’s probably fine, my mind keeps circling back to it.
Do you ever feel that things need to look or feel perfectly aligned, balanced, or 'just right,' even if there isn’t an obvious mistake or risk involved?

I’m not sure I’d say that, no. I mean, as a designer I do care about alignment and balance, but it feels more like part of the work than a separate “just right” feeling. I haven’t really noticed that outside of obvious design decisions.

Outside of your regular design work and the need to check for mistakes, have you ever felt that something needed to feel 'just right' in a way that went beyond normal design choices, like needing things to be perfectly aligned or balanced in a way that caused you distress?

No, I don’t think so. Outside of actual design work or checking for mistakes, I haven’t really noticed that kind of “just right” feeling causing me distress. It’s mostly tied to whether the work is correct or ready to send.
Have you ever had intrusive thoughts or felt the need to clean or wash something repeatedly because of worries about germs or contamination?
No, I haven’t really had that. I mean, I wash my hands normally, but I don’t get stuck on worries about germs or feel like I have to clean things over and over.

Within your work tasks, do you ever feel that things need to be arranged a certain way, or feel unsettled until something feels 'just right,' even if there’s no clear mistake or design rule that requires it?

Not really, no. If I’m arranging something, it’s usually because I’m trying to make the design work or meet the brief. I don’t think I get unsettled just because it doesn’t feel “just right” without a clear reason.

Have you ever experienced intrusive thoughts or felt the need to double-check things outside of your design work, even in everyday situations like making sure a door is locked or an appliance is turned off?
I don’t think so, no. I’ll check a door or the stove in the normal way, but I don’t get stuck going back over it again and again. At least, not that I’ve noticed.
